key_decisions: REVIEW CLOSURE (2026-10-21, binding): fix every confirmed finding — blocker, high, medium and low — before commit. Zero known defects at commit time. A deferral needs explicit user approval recorded in state/session-state.json with owner and rationale. A fix cycle revalidates the full gate; new findings count as new defects.

FEATURE PARITY (2026-10-21, binding): every user-facing function ships backend first, then frontend immediately in the same feature. No new feature until daemon and frontends reach functional parity. A daemon action without a frontend control is incomplete. Deferral only with explicit user approval recorded here.

UI REFERENCES (2026-10-21, binding): take interaction/layout patterns from cosmic-settings (native COSMIC structure), Webmin (dense module/action coverage), Cockpit (capability gating, status visibility, destructive confirmations). Copy patterns, not code; Ursine terminology and thin-frontend rules win.
No polkit: PAM handshake per session (daemon-side, service ursine, wheel check) then RAM-only Bearer session token. Web moves to OIDC later without API changes.
No database, daemon stateless: system is source of truth (apk/flatpak/nix/shadow/btrfs). Audit = JSONL + logrotate. Config = /etc/ursine/config.toml, tri-state auto|true|false.
Capabilities runtime-detected, never persisted; ensure_available() per request; capabilities.refresh + config.init APIs.
asUser param for per-user ops (flatpak --user, nix profile); default = principal; apk/--system always root.
Cargo features web/oidc trim binary (~2-3 MB) and idle RSS (~3-6 MB target); daemon always on via dinit, event-driven, no polling.
Modules v1: packages (nix first — unique gap), snapshots (owned by packages/store: manual + pre-update auto), users (accountsservice), niri config editor.
Do NOT build printers/scanners/bluetooth/network/firewall/disks — already packaged on Alpine (see docs/PROJECT.md).

Rust everywhere: GUI is libcosmic (COSMIC toolkit, iced-based Rust UI) — supersedes the GTK4/relm4 choice; shared serde types make a second backend language a liability. Web GUI must also be memory-safe (Rust→WASM preferred).

Build policy: musl everywhere incl. nix (pkgsMusl/pkgsStatic, never glibc). Local builds via Docker + Alpine images (rust:alpine). CI: test every cargo feature combination; build and publish nix flake (repo-resident, github:skea999/ursine; Release artifacts on tag).

Packaging (2026-10-20): release tarball owns install.sh + packaging/ (PAM + systemd/OpenRC/dinit). Installer needs root for /etc; Nix profile cannot install PAM/units, so NixOS needs a declarative module (not yet written) and non-NixOS uses the tarball installer. DESTDIR + explicit --init is the package-build path.
Agents wired: opencode.json instructions load CONTEXT/architecture/PROJECT/handoff/TASKS into every agent; .opencode/rules/ursine.md holds binding project invariants (via opencode-rules plugin).

INTENT CONFIRMED: version plan v1 (backend+GUI: nix, users, snapshots, niri) / v2 (apk, flatpak, printers, scanners, bluetooth, network, firewall, disks) / v3 (OIDC + web, LAST frontend) / v4 (Incus UI) / v5 (ZFS + Pirateus) / v6 (other distros). Phasing != exclusion: everything is in scope.

UI principles (binding, amended 2026-10-19): all UIs behave as one product (same layout/navigation/terminology; visual theme follows each toolkit — pixel-identical theming across toolkits NOT required, security wins) and must be user-friendly (COSMIC conventions, capability-gated panels never shown broken, confirm destructive actions, plain language).

CI FULLY CONTAINERIZED (skea999 correction): every GitHub Actions job runs in a Docker container — cargo matrix in alpine:3.22 (apk add rust cargo git nodejs; linux-pam-dev only on pam jobs), flake/release jobs in nixos/nix container. No rustup/cargo/nix ever installed on host runners.

Wayle shell remains GTK4 (C toolkit) by upstream choice — accepted risk; no migration planned upstream. GUI app avoids GTK. Web GUI memory-safe constraint must hold in v3 (Rust→WASM preferred).
GUI token risk: a compromised user-level process (or the GUI itself) could use the Bearer token until TTL expiry. Planned hardening: absolute token lifetime cap + PAM re-auth for destructive actions.
PAM relies on pam_unix + pam_acct_mgmt; no pam_faillock configured, daemon has only in-RAM rate limiting (5 failures/min).
Installer staged auth is fail-closed only when the target cannot execute: cross-arch packaging needs --allow-unverified-auth and remains unverified until the target runs.

Store GUI hardening is gate-green (143 tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt) but not visually smoked against a live daemon with a real nix profile. Long actions use a 1 s redraw tick; daemon limits are enforced. Smoke before release.
